paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different methods on BioMedLM, with “Base” representing the unedited model. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 35% to 65%, with major gridlines and tick labels every 5 percentage points. Six methods are plotted: “Base” (black solid line with circle markers) starts at ~38% and rises slightly to ~44%; “FT” (blue solid line with downward triangle markers) begins at ~40% and increases to ~48%; “IKE” (red solid line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~43% and climbs to ~49.5%; “MEND” (brown solid line with diamond markers) begins at ~44% and rises to ~56.5%; “MEMIT” (purple solid line with circle markers) starts at ~44% and increases to ~55%; and “ROME” (green solid line with square markers) begins at ~51% and steadily climbs to ~66%. All lines show a generally increasing trend as co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the range.
